statements.impact_statement: This CVE is in containerd's CRI checkpoint/restore plugin. In historical Helm 3 builds, containerd v1 was imported transitively through Helm's OCI registry client, but no operator binary ran a CRI server or checkpoint/restore operations. With the Helm 4.3.0 migration on 2026-10-02, github.com/containerd/containerd packages are absent from go list -deps ./... and are no longer built into any operator binary. The module remains in the module graph only through operator-registry's own image package tests (go mod why -m github.com/containerd/containerd), which are not part of this operator's binaries. These versioned VEX products are retained for historical builds and module-level scanners.

This CVE is in containerd's CRI checkpoint-import path. Historical Helm 3 builds used only generic OCI client code and never ran a CRI server or checkpoint/restore operations. Since the Helm 4.3.0 migration on 2026-10-02, no github.com/containerd/containerd packages are in the operator binaries' dependency graph (go list -deps ./...). The module remains only through operator-registry's own tests, not operator production code. See the CVE-2026-53492 statement for the module-level dependency chain; versioned VEX products remain applicable to historical builds and module-level scanners.

This advisory flags golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp and its subpackages as unmaintained and unsafe by design, with no fixed version. Historical Helm 3 builds imported these packages transitively through Helm's chart provenance feature, but the operator never called that feature. Since the Helm 4.3.0 migration on 2026-10-02, golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp and its subpackages are absent from go list -deps ./... and are no longer built into any operator binary. The versioned VEX product is retained for historical builds.
